chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Al-Tatarri from them (the narrators) from Abdullah ibn Muskam from Mansur ibn Hazim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who plucked the arak trees in Mecca. He said: 'He must pay its price.' And he said: 'Nothing is removed from the trees of Mecca except dates and fruit trees.'

key_terms.الْأَرَاكِ: Arak trees (specifically the shade-providing trees in Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a pilgrim who plucks trees in Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial compensation (thaman) required for a pilgrim who plucks vegetation in the Haram, establishing a general rule of liability with a specific exception for date palms and fruit trees. This ruling highlights the sanctity of Mecca's flora, distinguishing between general shrubs (arak) and valuable agricultural produce, thereby guiding pilgrims on preserving the ecological and spiritual integrity of the sacred precincts during Hajj.
